55_sea_lettuce.desc: Often found in nutrient rich or even polluted areas in the wild. Suitable for temperate or tropical conditions.
56_eel_grass.desc: Dense beds of this grass create the perfect habitat for delicate slow-moving animals including seahorses, pipefish and seadragons.
57_kelp.desc: This giant seaweed creates underwater forests perfect for larger fish and sharks. Species of kelp can grow up to half a meter daily, reaching up to 80m in height.
42_feather_calurpa.desc: This algae sends out chains of runners that attach to rocks and substrate. Shoots of feathery foliage grow from all angles of the runners.
43_triangle_turbinweed.desc: Found on the outer reef flats where it is exposed to strong surge, Turbinweed is tough.
44_asparagus_weed.desc: This seaweed with its fluffy swaying branches could be mistaken for a coral. Asparagus Weed is popularly eaten in Hawaii, principally as a condiment.
58_egg_wrack.desc: The “eggs” of Egg Wrack are actually capsules of floating air that enable this seaweed to stand vertically and reach as much light as possible.
73_sea_grapes.desc: Sea Grapes taste as good as they look and can be eaten.
74_velvet_horn.desc: Found in deep tidal pools. The leaves have a felt-like texture.
75_rubberweed.desc: So toughened and rubbery, it's hard to detach from rocks.
76_chain_halimeda.desc: Found on shady coral slopes, the discs form chains of 50cm.
77_shellweed.desc: This distinctively shaped weed is calcareous making it hard and brittle.
3_small_rock.desc: Rocks provide a surface for microscopic bacteria and zoo plankton to live on. This 'live' surface lends a small amount of filtering to the tank.
60_rubble.desc: This large field of rocks provides additional filtering and a place for certain fish to hide and play.
51_small_live_rock.desc: Live Rocks arrive with a full complement of zoo plankton already on them. The result: better filtration right out of the box!
52_large_live_rock.desc: This large field of live rocks provides the perfect place for small fish to forage and play.
53_driftwood_cave.desc: This carelessly strewn driftwood forms the perfect shelter for small cave loving animals.
45_rocky_overhang.desc: This rocky tunnel provides a larger shelter for cave loving animals.
54_pitted_column.desc: The Pitted Column is perfect for deep tanks which house many cave loving animals.
62_gaping_cavern.desc: The Gaping Cavern provides a shelter for the largest of cave loving animals.
